--- MCP.md ---
Tools | Desktop
SilverBullet Desktop serves MCP too, for the spaces registered in the app, on a loopback listener at `http://127.0.0.1:3999/.mcp`. It is off by default. Turn it on or change the port under **Settings → Advanced → MCP**, which also shows the setup commands with your port filled in.

--- CHANGELOG.md ---
CHANGELOG | Edge
* [[MCP]]: SilverBullet Server can now serve an MCP endpoint at `/.mcp`, so AI assistants can directly read, write, search and query your spaces. Clients sign in with OAuth and act as the account that approved them, on the spaces chosen on a consent page. MCP is off by default: an admin turns it on in the APIs tab.
* **Potentially breaking:** the legacy `/.auth/authorize` and `/.auth/token` endpoints now only accept SilverBullet’s own clients (`silverbullet-app`, `silverbullet-cli` and `silverbullet-share`); other `client_id`s are refused.
* Fix: slow filesystem watcher registration no longer delays space startup. Polling tracks changes while native notifications start, and a resync reconciles changes made during registration.

--- MCP.md ---
Tools
SilverBullet can act as an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (Model Context Protocol) server, so AI assistants can read, write, query and pimp up your spaces.

MCP is available in [[Dashboard|multi-space mode]] and in [[Desktop]]. The endpoint is `/.mcp` on your server, for example `https://notes.example.com/.mcp`. A single-space server does not serve it. On a server it is off by default: an admin turns it on in the APIs tab of the [[Dashboard]].

--- TLS.md ---
LAN HTTP (no TLS) | localhost (http)
If you run SilverBullet _locally_ on your machine, this is the easiest option. Everything runs fine as long as the browser sees `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` appear in the URL, even with `http://`.

The obvious drawback of this approach is that your SilverBullet instance is _only accessible from the machine you run it on_.

--- Install/Desktop.md ---
Download
SilverBullet Desktop runs on macOS, Windows and Linux.
